solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Less rapid fluid distribution

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed in shape, so the letters of the two words before it flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Something spreads out more slowly, like a liquid moving at a gentler pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less rapid fluid' reads as a description of a sluggish liquid; 'fluid' is the anagram signal working on LESSRAPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersal is the act of spreading things widely, which is what distribution means.

clue.text: Prepare fish? Fresh eels and dace, mostly

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are rearranged into a new word
mostly means most but not all of the word dace, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A fishmonger readies the catch: some fresh eels and most of a dace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts dace to DAC; 'Fresh' then shuffles EELS plus DAC. The question mark flags that descaling is only one way to prepare a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the scales is a standard step when a cook gets a fish ready for the pan.

clue.text: Guard spotted protecting both ends of corridor

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: spotted means seen

indicators.note: both ends of means the first and last letters of the word corridor

explanation.surface: A security guard is seen keeping watch over the ends of a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard' could be a noun in the surface, but the answer works as the verb: to screen is to shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen shields or protects something, so as a verb it means to guard.

clue.text: Boredom reining us in from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means only now and then, so every other letter of the words reining us in is taken

explanation.surface: Tedium occasionally holds us back and keeps us in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' takes the even letters of REININGUSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan word for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a synonym of boredom.

clue.text: Replacement transport heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so it is backwards

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A replacement bus service travels northbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns BUS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub, short for substitute, is a replacement player or person.

clue.text: Vigorously enjoy vintage footwear?

parts.note: to enjoy something is to like it
vintage means old
boots are footwear

explanation.surface: Someone is a big fan of old-fashioned shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the surface reading is a literal take on a British idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The British informal phrase 'like old boots' means with great energy or force, as in working hard.

clue.text: Rope caught with skill

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
someone able has skill

explanation.surface: A rope is lassoed or grabbed deftly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a thick, strong rope, as used for mooring ships.

clue.text: Fail to show up a hairdresser?

parts.note: to show up is to come
a cropper is one who crops, here someone who cuts hair short

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hairdresser failed to turn up for an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail to show up' reads as one phrase about absence; the definition is only 'Fail'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is an informal British idiom for falling heavily or suffering a failure.

clue.text: Playful banter is hurtful in time

parts.note: bad can mean harmful or hurtful
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Teasing chatter can turn wounding over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, witty exchange of teasing remarks, which is banter.

clue.text: Antelope born right at the end of season

indicators.note: at the end of places the following pieces after the season word

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
OK means right or correct

explanation.surface: A young antelope is born just as one season closes.
explanation.definitionFit: The springbok is a southern African gazelle-like antelope known for leaping.

clue.text: Area of France featuring in some documentaries

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so the letters run across the words some documentaries

explanation.surface: A French region appears in several documentary films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring in' signals the run of letters across soME DOCumentaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Médoc is a wine-producing district of south-west France near Bordeaux.

clue.text: On camera I prepared a hot drink

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or put together, so the letters of the preceding words are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A TV cook, filmed, makes a cup of something hot.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a common coffee drink.

clue.text: Lops head off plant

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts the top off a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lops head off' reads as pruning; 'off' is the anagram signal on LOPSHEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily-family flower, in Greek myth said to cover the fields of the underworld.

clue.text: Yellow bird at front of cage

indicators.note: at front of means the first letter of the word cage is taken

parts.note: a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: A yellow bird sits at the front of its cage, perhaps a canary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' suggests a canary; here it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means contemptibly lacking courage.

clue.text: Stolen files ultimately erased

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of the word files is taken

parts.note: erased means wiped

explanation.surface: Computer files were stolen and then wiped from the drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To swipe is informal for to steal, so swiped means stolen.

clue.text: Was hiding in this place, however

indicators.note: hiding means concealing something within, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: in this place means here

explanation.surface: Someone was hiding here all along, though.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' looks like part of the story but is the insertion signal; 'in this place' is one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereas introduces a contrast, as 'however' or 'while on the other hand' does.

clue.text: Detectives carrying around a bug

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
CA is circa, Latin for around, used before dates

explanation.surface: Police detectives carry around a listening bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests a listening device but means an insect; CA (circa) is the usual Latin abbreviation for around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a loud chirping insect, and bug is a common word for insect.

clue.text: State of heightened activity concerning campaign push

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a drive is an organised campaign or push towards a goal

explanation.surface: A heightened state of activity surrounds a big push in a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in overdrive means working at an intense, frantic level beyond the normal.

clue.text: Pipe close to overhead shower

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so the last letter of the word overhead is taken

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: A pipe runs close to an overhead shower head in a bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe or channel carrying away waste water.

clue.text: Took horse round for cowboy event

parts.note: to take horse is to ride, so took horse means rode
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A rider took a horse around the arena at a cowboy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a contest where cowboys show skills such as bronco riding and roping.

clue.text: Rugby player tucked in, devouring a good spread

indicators.note: devouring means taking inside, so the last pieces go within the first two

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
to tuck in is to eat heartily, so tucked in means ate

explanation.surface: A hungry rugby player wolfs down a fine buffet spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a meal but is a verb; 'devouring' sets the a-plus-good pair between the player and the eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to spread or disseminate something, such as ideas or plants.

clue.text: Electrical unit erected inside farmhouse

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down entry the letters are read from the bottom up
inside means the letters are found within the word farmhouse

explanation.surface: An electrical unit was installed in a farmhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' picks MHO from farMHOuse; 'erected' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Reference book finally abridged

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: A reference work has at last been published in a shortened edition.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, a standard work of reference.

clue.text: Europeans from San Marino, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters of San Marino

explanation.surface: Some Europeans might come from San Marino.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanians are citizens of Romania, a country in eastern Europe.
